title: Salvation in Christ Alone
definition: Salvation in Christ Alone means sinners are saved only through the person and work of Jesus Christ, not through any other mediator, system, or merit.
summary: Salvation in Christ Alone means sinners are saved only through the person and work of Jesus Christ, not through any other mediator, system, or merit.
christFocus: Jesus is the only Savior, the only mediator, and the only way to the Father.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture teaches that salvation is found in Christ alone. No religious effort, moral record, spiritual experience, human leader, or personal suffering can take the place of the Savior God has given.

Christ alone can save because Christ alone is the incarnate Son, sinless substitute, risen Lord, and faithful mediator. He does not merely show one path among many; He is the way to the Father.

This doctrine centers the heart on Jesus. Every blessing of salvation—forgiveness, righteousness, adoption, new life, peace, and final hope—comes through union with Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often look for rescue in self-improvement, religion, relationships, substances, approval, or spiritual experiences. Salvation in Christ alone lovingly closes every false door so the sinner may run to the only Savior who can truly save.

This also keeps ministry from becoming personality-centered. The hope we offer is not a program, platform, or teacher, but Jesus Christ Himself.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Place your confidence in Christ alone. Reject every false savior, receive the grace He gives, and point others clearly to Jesus rather than to yourself, your story, or your ministry as the source of hope.
